title: Aspects of Traditional Culture in the County.
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Ask learners to bring or describe an object, food or song from home. Treat every community's culture with respect and never rank them.

skills.key_step: The child sorts examples into the aspects of traditional culture (dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, festivals and ceremonies) and knows culture is alive and differs between communities.

floor.prerequisite: Names a cultural event in the community.
floor.question: Name one ceremony held in your community.
floor.answer: any ceremony such as a wedding or a naming

representations: six boxes labelled with the aspects
a song or a game from a community
steps: Ask: is it worn, eaten, lived in, made, played or celebrated?
Ask whether people still use it today.
contexts: a beaded necklace from a Maasai home
a bao game under a tree

board.do: Write the six aspects across the board.

board.say: Is a drum worn, eaten or made by hand?

board.do: Ask where a wedding dance goes before writing it.

misconceptions.ask: Under which aspect of culture is a kiondo (a sisal basket)?
misconceptions.repair: Make six boxes, one for each aspect, and sort a pile of picture cards.

misconceptions.ask: Is traditional culture still practised today?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which dishes, songs and ceremonies the family still shares.

listen_for: Yes, they all do the same things
misconceptions.ask: Do all the communities in a county have the same traditions?
misconceptions.repair: Ask each learner to name one dish, dance or dress from their own community.

listen_for: Yes, it should all be stopped
misconceptions.ask: A learner says all traditional culture is backward. What is a good reply?
misconceptions.repair: List good parts of culture the class still enjoys: food, songs, games, respect for elders.

checks.question: Under which aspect does a traditional stool go?
Do all communities in a county have the same traditions?
checks.answer: No, communities have their own traditions
